items.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: And I think now my daughters, I have Sophie and Vivian

ctx.x: So you were surrounded by that in your house as you grew up, that music.

Yes. Certainly that energy. My father was composing, sitting at the piano composing, and there were many well known songwriters and lyricists who would come by our place. So I took that all pretty much for granted. They were just — kids don’t know any of that sort of stuff. And I think now my daughters, I have Sophie and Vivian, Vivian’s only seven months old at the time of this taping, Sophie is almost three years old. And they’ve met many very important jazz musicians through their life, but they don’t know it,…
That’s great. Can you describe your improvising? I ask this question a lot and I get a lot of different answers. But the thought process that happens when you’re improvising?
